subject: SequenceLock: Model16b p95 latency breach & rollback approval
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@streamline.ai>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Increased latency on Model16b – production impact

Monica,

Quick flag from our side: starting ~08:50 PT we observed p95 latency on the /generate endpoint backed by model16b jump from ~320ms to ~1.8s across multiple regions. This spike is impacting our real-time chat threads — customer complaints are trickling in. The spike correlates with the rollout of variant "16b-v3-canary" per the headers we capture.

Attached: p95_dashboard.png (screenshot of Grafana showing p95 by region).

Can you confirm if you see the same on your side? We need a fast remediation plan — happy to take a scheduled rollback if that’s easiest to restore SLA. This is a high-priority production incident for us.

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Head of Platform — StreamlineAI
ops@streamline.ai

--
Please keep security logs intact; we have compliance windows for our customers.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc:
Date: 2028-05-23T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Increased latency on Model16b – production impact

Forwarding Samir's note — StreamlineAI is seeing a p95 surge that lines up with 16b-v3-canary traffic. I pulled a quick summary from our monitoring:
- Customer: StreamlineAI (account id: 12345)
- Model: model16b, active variant: 16b-v3-canary
- Observed: p95 across N. Virginia and us-west-2 rose to ~1.6–1.9s starting ~08:50 PT; baseline p95 ~300ms
- Impact: chat throughput degraded, user complaints reported

Ask: Rishi, can you triage and propose immediate remediation — prefer a rollback of the canary or a traffic-split rollback for this account if that's lower-risk.
Ben — I need authorization to do a customer-targeted rollback and a short SLA carveout (up to 30 mins) while we stabilize. If you approve, I’ll: 1) notify the customer of the planned rollback window, 2) execute a targeted traffic shift back to 16b-v2-stable, 3) post a Mutual Action Plan (attached) and schedule follow-ups.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.docx

-Monica

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-23T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Increased latency on Model16b – production impact

Quick triage summary:
- Root cause hypothesis: kernel scheduling mismatch combined with KV-cache fragmentation on the new 16b-v3 quantized path. Canary uses a different memory layout and we see CPU-side stalls when real-time batching patterns change.
- Evidence: stack traces + rollout metadata (attached rollback_patch.diff) and realtime logs from the serving nodes.
- Risk assessment: rollback to 16b-v2-stable for StreamlineAI only is low risk (no model re-compilation). Full rollback cluster-wide will take ~10–12 minutes with a brief spike on warm-up; customer-targeted traffic split is immediate (config change).
- Recommended action: perform a target traffic reweight to route StreamlineAI back to 16b-v2-stable (no code redeploy). Post-mortem to follow; prepare patch that fixes memory alignment for v3.

If we get approval, I’ll stage the traffic change and monitor p95 for the next 30 minutes. I’ve attached rollback_patch.diff for the follow-on fix; that will require a low-impact maintenance window to ship.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
